original_question: Let Gamma be a numerical semigroup, let Gamma_tilde be its interval completion, and let R_Gamma = k[[Gamma]] and R_{Gamma_tilde} = k[[Gamma_tilde}] be the corresponding local semigroup rings. Is it true for every homological degree i that the Betti numbers of the local semigroup ring do not decrease under interval completion, i.e. b_i(R_Gamma) <= b_i(R_{Gamma_tilde}) for all i?
target_in_paper: Section 3 (Width), Problem 12: the interval-completion monotonicity question for all Betti numbers of the semigroup ring.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the main mathematical content of the target problem very well: it uses a numerical semigroup Γ, its interval completion Γ̃, the local semigroup rings k[[Γ]] and k[[Γ̃]], and asks whether the Betti numbers are monotone in the direction Γ -> Γ̃ for every homological degree. That is exactly the nearby official question asked in Section 3, Problem 12.
missing_details: The paper fixes a field K and suppresses it from later notation; for higher Betti numbers, the answer can depend on the characteristic of K, so the field should be declared fixed (or quantified).
The interval completion should be defined explicitly in the paper’s notation: if Γ = ⟨n1 < ··· < ne⟩ is minimally generated in increasing order, then Γ̃ := ⟨n1, n1+1, ..., ne⟩.
The paper’s notation is βi(Γ), not bi(RΓ).
The Betti numbers are those of the semigroup ring with respect to a minimal regular presentation.
The equivalence between local and graded semigroup ring Betti numbers is implicit in your draft but explicit in the paper: βi(K[Γ]) = βi(K[[Γ]]) for all i.

The quantifier is simply 'for all i'; there is no asymptotic clause or degree restriction. Since β0 = 1 on both sides, the substantive content begins at i >= 1, but the paper states the question for all i.
To make the question fully stand-alone, it helps to say that a numerical semigroup is a cofinite additive submonoid of N.
The width context is implicit in your draft: interval completion is introduced in Section 3 because it preserves the width while enlarging the generating interval.
refined_question: Fix a field K. Let Γ = ⟨n1 < ··· < ne⟩ ⊆ N be a numerical semigroup (that is, a cofinite additive submonoid of N), and let its interval completion be Γ̃ := ⟨n1, n1+1, ..., ne⟩. Write βi(Γ) := βi(K[[Γ]]) for the i-th Betti number of the local semigroup ring of Γ. Is it true that βi(Γ) <= βi(Γ̃) for every homological degree i >= 0?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, since the paper recalls that βi(K[Γ]) = βi(K[[Γ]]) for all i, one may ask whether βi(K[Γ]) <= βi(K[Γ̃]) for every i >= 0.
justification: The draft matches Section 3, Problem 12, not the neighboring Problem 13. Section 3 first introduces interval completion in the fixed-width discussion, then asks the monotonicity question for higher Betti numbers under interval completion. Section 1 supplies the hidden notation needed to make the problem stand-alone: the local semigroup ring is K[[Γ]], Betti numbers are defined via minimal regular presentations, and for numerical semigroups the Betti numbers of K[Γ] and K[[Γ]] agree in every homological degree. So the paper-faithful refinement is the local/graded semigroup-ring interval-completion monotonicity question stated above.
